newsitem.title: USA: Pacific Intertie rate increase expected by Monday.
newsitem.headline: Pacific Intertie rate increase expected by Monday.

text.p: Capacity on the Pacific Intertie should be raised by 600 megawatts (MW) to 6,900 MW no later than 2400 PDT on Monday, a spokeswoman for the Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) said Tuesday.

The increase in the interstate transmission system's capacity was approved by the Western Systems Coordinating Council (WSCC) last week, but review of necessary operating procedures is still underway.
BPA said the review has been complicated by repair work at the Bonneville dam in Oregon, which has heightened the risk of a line outage upstream of that project, along the John Day cut plain.
"They (the WSCC study group) will meet Thursday and Friday to discuss it," said a spokeswoman for the WSCC.
The BPA spokeswoman said the agency remained hopeful of final clearance by Monday.
The Intertie's current 6,300 MW rating will expire Thursday, but the WSCC spokeswoman said that limit would likely be extended if the new rating is not implemented by then.
